audit.why: Emerald+ 51.54% over 487 games — the smallest sample in this slice but the figure matches the table.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats Body Slam as an unavoidable engage and never mentions that it stops on the first unit it touches.
audit.why: Kit text: "Gragas charges to a location and collides with the first enemy unit he comes across." Standing with a minion between you and Gragas means his engage dies on the caster wave. For a champion with no dash and no escape this is the most useful single fact in the matchup, and it is absent from every field.
audit.corrected: Added to content.early and the full-layer cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Body Slam is named as the tracked cooldown but never numbered.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s — it barely improves with rank, so it is effectively a 12-14s window all game. That is long enough to run a full stack-and-swallow sequence inside, which is exactly the plan the entry keeps hinting at without the number to justify it.
audit.corrected: Figure added to content.mid, whys[3] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere in the content layer despite Happy Hour being a heal-on-every-cast passive.
audit.why: Happy Hour heals Gragas each time he uses a skill, which is precisely what breaks Tahm Kench's grind-them-down plan. The entry describes "his Q sustain" without naming the passive that actually provides it, and never tells the player to buy Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour named and Grievous Wounds called for in whys[3], whys[6], mid and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry credits Tahm Kench with "Abyssal Voyage" 2 time(s) and treats it as a global/roaming ultimate.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage was removed in the Tahm Kench rework. The kit file lists W = Abyssal Dive and R = Devour; there is no global travel ability in the kit at all. Advice built on "use Abyssal Voyage to roam / reposition cross-map" tells the player to press a button that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed to Devour (R) or Abyssal Dive (W) as appropriate, with the surrounding advice rewritten so it describes what those abilities actually do.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly sells a "Q-stun then Devour" chain as one combo.
audit.why: Riot's own text in the kit: An Acquired Taste — "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion"; Tongue Lash — "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." The stun and the swallow draw on the same three stacks, so a Q cast at 3 stacks stuns and destroys the resource Devour requires. The real sequence is to let Q land the THIRD stack (which does not stun) and then press R.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as: build to three, let Q apply the third stack, Devour immediately; a Q thrown at an enemy already on 3 stacks stuns but burns the swallow.

edits.before: Gragas at levels 1-3 wants to shove Barrel Roll Q into the minion wave, sustain off it, and Body Slam into you for a short burst trade before you reach 3 stacks. Your job is to use Tongue Lash's range to fish for stacks on the approach — tag him twice with Q and an auto, then the moment he Body Slams in, the third hit is already loaded and the stun lands before he can disengage. Do not stand in his Q pool after a Body Slam; he delays his W until you are inside the barrel and it shreds your health bar faster than grey health builds. The lane is genuinely even here — he has sustain, you have sustain, and the player who lands their setup first gets the first real trade win.
edits.after: Gragas at levels 1-3 wants to shove Barrel Roll Q into the minion wave, sustain off it, and Body Slam into you for a short burst trade before you reach 3 stacks. Body Slam stops on the first unit it hits, so keep a minion between you — then tag him twice from range and let Q land the third stack as he commits, because a Q at 3 stuns and burns what Devour needs. Do not stand in his Q pool after a Body Slam; he delays his W until you are inside the barrel and it shreds your health bar faster than grey health builds. The lane is genuinely even here — he has sustain, you have sustain, and the player who lands their setup first gets the first real trade win.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are Gragas's quiet comfort zone and your most vulnerable window: no Abyssal Voyage means he can Body Slam away from any 3-stack attempt, and his Q sustain keeps him healthy through your poke. Play for CS, not kills — use Tongue Lash to shove the wave and force him to Q minions rather than you, burning his stack-fishing cooldown on last-hits. At 6 the dynamic shifts against you: his Explosive Cask has range to interrupt your Devour mid-animation, and a well-timed R can knock you backwards just as you commit your stun. Use your own Abyssal Voyage to exit a bad fight rather than as aggression; his barrel has more solo-kill setup potential than your kit in this window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Gragas's comfort zone and your most vulnerable window: with no ultimate yet he can still Body Slam away from any 3-stack attempt on its flat 14s cooldown, and Happy Hour heals him on every cast. Play for CS, not kills — use Tongue Lash to shove the wave and force him to Q minions rather than you, burning his stack-fishing cooldown on last-hits. At 6 the dynamic shifts against you: his Explosive Cask has range to interrupt your Devour mid-animation, and a well-timed R can knock you backwards just as you commit your stun. Use your own Devour on the ally he casks rather than as aggression; Explosive Cask has more solo-kill setup potential than your kit in this window.

edits.before: At 3 An Acquired Taste stacks your Tongue Lash stuns Gragas in place — the one window his Body Slam dash cannot save him from the Devour follow-up.
edits.after: Let Tongue Lash land the third An Acquired Taste stack and Devour on the spot — Body Slam cannot outrun it, but a Q at 3 stuns and consumes the stacks.

edits.before: He has no ultimate yet and your Devour combo is live, but his Q sustain and the Body Slam reset make clean 3-stack attempts risky — farm, whittle, and wait for Voyage.
edits.after: He has no ultimate yet and your Devour combo is live, but Happy Hour's heal on every cast and Body Slam's 14s exit make clean 3-stack attempts risky — bring Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: At 2+ items both Thick Skin and his W damage reduction make trades attritional — whoever stacks displacement onto the other first (your stun-Devour or his Body Slam-Cask) controls the outcome.
edits.after: At 2+ items both Thick Skin and his W damage reduction make trades attritional — whoever lands first (your third stack into Devour, or his Body Slam-Cask) controls it — and anti-heal is mandatory.

edits.before: Stack An Acquired Taste to 3 on Gragas and land the Tongue Lash stun before he can Body Slam away
edits.after: Stack An Acquired Taste to 3 on Gragas and swallow him on the third stack, before Body Slam is back

edits.before: Sustain through your poke with Barrel Roll Q pools and sit on grey health without giving you a clean 3-stack window
edits.after: Heal off Happy Hour on every cast and chip your grey-health bank down without giving you a clean 3-stack window

edits.before: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — His engage. W-dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — 14s, stops on minions. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Body Slam stopping on the first unit it touches is the fact this entry most needed and did not have. Smallest sample in the slice (487 games) — treat the 51.54% as soft.
